A little beyond the soft ring of light cast by the near-spent candles can be heard the whispering crush of leaves and brushing of grass. A small child dances about in a flowing gown trimmed in flowers, embroidered or perhaps growing. The light slowly reveals a summoning. Pausing for a moment at the offering the dress-clad dancer scrunches a nose at the wine then places a small silver coin beside the bottle. More footfalls, rather the sound of hooves, herald a visitor. A donkey saunters in from the darkness. The child pauses their dance to show the animal the coin.
“Good likeness, I remember you then” the donkey says while inspecting the goat-legged drunkard depicted on the coin. The child goes back to dancing, pocketing the coin somewhere in the folds of their dress.
